archetypes.name: bash-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes 30+ specific behavioral claims about rebase-push.sh, run_rebase_rebump, auto-resolve-changelog.sh, and git-sync-local-main.sh that must be verified against the actual bash scripts before implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the bash scripts referenced in the plan (rebase-push.sh, the run_rebase_rebump function in ship-pr.sh, auto-resolve-changelog.sh, git-sync-local-main.sh) and check each specific behavioral claim: the --allow-changelog-only --max-depth 20 argument shape, PUSH_REMOTE resolution order (pushRemote -> remote -> origin), EXPECTED_REMOTE_OID computed once across retries rather than refreshed, the rebase pre-pass --ours rule for plugin.json/version.go/go.sum, and the _max_rebases bash variable value versus the plan's REBASE_MAX_ATTEMPTS=20. Flag any plan claim that does not match what the bash code actually does, any logic present in bash that the plan omits entirely, and any bash line references (e.g., ~3034-3071 for the version-regression guard) where the described Python logic diverges from the real implementation. Pay special attention to whether the companion CHANGELOG drop in bash uses a versioned form or a generic subject-depth replay, since the plan's correctness argument for preventing #2952 depends on this distinction. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: phase-api-surface
archetypes.rationale: The plan calls many Phase 1/2 functions with specific signatures; any parameter mismatch makes the new module uncompilable without changes to upstream modules that are out of scope for Phase 3.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the Python scope files (python/changelog.py, python/version_bump.py, python/git.py, python/agents.py, python/config.py) and verify every function call the plan proposes against its actual current signature. Check: version_bump.drop_bump_commit with allow_changelog_only and max_depth params, changelog.auto_resolve, changelog.extract_version_body, changelog.drop_changelog_commit with an old_version positional argument, changelog.duplicate_version_heading_count, changelog.write_changelog_entry, changelog.commit_changelog with replaces_version, and agents.run_waterfall with a first_tier keyword. Verify whether each constant the plan references but does not add (DROP_CHANGELOG_MAX_DEPTH, ENV_IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR, BUMP_COMMIT_SUBJECT_TEMPLATE, LARCH_BUMP_FILES, FIXER_TIER_ORDER) already exists in config.py with the expected name and type, since the plan's config.py update section only lists REBASE_MAX_ATTEMPTS and FIXER_ROLE as additions. Flag parameter-name mismatches, missing positional arguments, or any call site where the plan's proposed invocation shape cannot work with the existing function definition. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-gap-map
archetypes.rationale: The plan's Edge Cases and Failure Modes sections list behaviors with no obvious corresponding named test case, leaving parity gaps that could ship undetected through the stub-runner harness.
archetypes.prompt_body: Map each item in the Edge Cases and Failure Modes sections of the plan to a named test case in the test_rebase.py test list and identify any that are undercovered. Flag edge cases described in prose but absent from the named test cases: fork-mode PUSH_REMOTE differing from base_remote, the _sync_local_main refuse-when-current-branch-is-main guard, drop_bump_commit benign no-match vs real-error branching distinction, and the lease-rejected-but-remote-tip-already-equals-HEAD short-circuit success path. Check whether the stub runner pattern is sufficient to exercise _changelog_ready_after_rebump's three-condition check (new heading present, no stale old heading when versions differ, CHANGELOG.md porcelain-clean) without a real git working tree, or whether the plan's stub design would pass these conditions vacuously. Also verify the test list covers the no-CHANGELOG-tail failure mode (apply_bump succeeds but _commit_changelog_after_rebump finds nothing staged and replaces_version fallback is also absent) and the stale-bump replay loop detection path that the plan cites as a critical mitigation for the #2952 class of bugs. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
